teaching.hint: Would reaching the same position after a forward jump and after a backward jump leave the same next moves?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Position alone is insufficient state: whether the previous jump went backward changes the legal next transitions.
solution_outline.approach: Search states consisting of position and last-jump direction in increasing jump count. Discard forbidden or negative positions and cap the positive search at a bound derived from the largest relevant coordinate plus one possible overshoot and return.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A state is visited once per direction flag, and its recorded level is the smallest jump count reaching it.
solution_outline.correctness: Every legal jump from every relevant state is considered, while illegal consecutive backward jumps are excluded. A shortest path need not travel beyond the derived bound in an obstacle-free suffix, so breadth-first levels find the minimum or establish impossibility.
solution_outline.complexity: O(U+f) time and space, where U=max(x,max forbidden)+a+b≤6000 and f is the number of forbidden positions.
solution_outline.pitfall: Marking only positions as visited can discard a later arrival with a different legal next move.

common_wrong_turns: Ignore the previous-jump direction in visited state
source_fidelity_notes: The no-consecutive-backward rule, overshoot permission, position bounds, and x=0 case are retained.
